A curtain of pale green aurora ripples silently across the night sky behind her, its slow pulse casting fleeting emerald light across the snowfield below.
Distant god-rays pierce a bruised stormfront on the horizon, illuminating a single ruined spire rising from the valley mist like a finger pointing skyward.
A vast dragon-shadow glides across the underbelly of the cloud layer overhead, its wingspan stretching from ridge to ridge before dissolving into grey.
Rolling fog pours down the mountain slopes like slow water, swallowing the pine forests below and leaving only the highest peaks visible above the white.
A burning watchtower flares orange on a distant hilltop, its signal fire sending a thick black column of smoke bending westward in the high wind.
Fey lights drift lazily through the treeline behind him, pale gold and wandering, flickering between trunks like lanterns carried by unseen hands deeper into the wood.
A portal shimmers on the far ridge, its oval frame crackling with cold blue light, the landscape visible through it subtly wrong — the sky there is red.
Cathedral clouds tower above the valley, their inner chambers lit by slow golden shafts that fall in great columns across the distant river far below.
A leyline scar splits the hillside visible across the gorge, the earth there glowing faint amber, the grass growing in strange symmetrical patterns along its length.
A meteor trails a long white scar across the dusk sky, burning slow and steady from horizon to horizon before winking out above the dark treeline.
Unnatural mist clings to the crown of the far mountain despite clear skies everywhere else, rotating slowly, the peaks inside it periodically lit by sourceless white light.
A waterfall plunges off an impossible cliff face in the background, its scale dwarfing the forest below, the mist at its base catching the low sun in a permanent rainbow.
The forest stream behind her glows a steady copper-gold beneath the surface, its light moving upstream against the current, lighting the moss on the bank from below.
Storm-clouds mass on the eastern horizon in the shape of an enormous face, its features shifting as the winds reshape them — recognisable for a moment, then gone.
A second pale moon hangs visible in the late afternoon sky, smaller and too close, its surface texture wrong — scored with long straight lines like old wounds.
Snow falls upward from the frozen lake behind him, lifted by some invisible force, spiralling lazily toward a break in the clouds overhead in a slow column.
Three distant peaks are connected by arcing threads of lightning that do not dissipate, holding steady between the summits like a bridge of white fire in the storm.
A procession of ghostly lights moves along the far ridge in silence, spaced evenly, too large to be torches, drifting at walking pace southward through the dark.
The old forest on the valley floor is lit from within by a deep amber glow, the light pulsing slowly outward from a hidden centre like a sleeping heartbeat.
Smoke rises from seven separate points across the plains below in perfect geometric arrangement, each column rising straight despite the wind, connected by faint lines on the earth.
The river in the gorge below runs backwards, its surface churning against the rock, the sound of it reaching her as a low continuous thunder from far below.
An aurora bleeds down to the treeline on the far slope, unusually low, its green and white curtains brushing the uppermost branches of the ancient oaks below.
A enormous stone arch on the distant hillside frames a sky that does not match — through its span the stars are visible in full dark despite the midday sun.
Ice formations have grown overnight across the far cliff face into the unmistakable shape of enormous antlers, catching the morning light and scattering it across the snow below.
The horizon beyond the battlefield glows deep red beneath a clear sky, the light sourceless and steady, silhouetting the broken treeline in sharp black against the burning distance.

A great dragon's shadow sweeps silently across the distant cloud-layer, vast and unhurried, its wingtips briefly darkening the far hillside before the sky swallows it whole, leaving only a trembling stillness and the faint smell of sulfur drifting on the wind.

God-rays lance downward through a breach in the storm-clouds ahead, illuminating a single ruined tower on the ridge in pale gold light while everything surrounding it churns in violet shadow, as though some divine attention has paused there and not yet moved on.

The aurora has descended lower than auroras should, rippling curtains of emerald and bone-white rolling slowly above the treeline, close enough that the leaves beneath them shimmer with reflected color, the whole sky humming at a frequency felt more in the chest than heard.

A leyline scar has opened across the valley floor, a luminous crack of cold blue light etched into the earth for half a mile, too straight to be natural, older than any road, pulsing faintly in a slow rhythm like something enormous breathing underground.

Somewhere deep in the forest across the river, the trees are glowing — not burning, but emanating a steady amber warmth from root to canopy, the light spilling outward across the water's surface in long wavering threads, drawing moths and silence in equal measure.
